heard: NASA intentionally crashed a $3 billion spacecraft into Saturn's crushing atmosphere. The Cassini-Huygens mission, a joint international effort, arrived at the ringed planet in July 2004. The spacecraft discovered geysers of water ice on Enceladus and methane seas on the massive moon Titan. These worlds had everything needed for life, but Cassini was running out of rocket fuel. Scientists realized if the dead probe ever drifted and crashed, earthly microbes could contaminate these pristine moons. To prevent a biological disaster, they ordered a grand finale, dive through the rings and into Saturn's clouds. On September 15, 2017, Cassini fought Saturn's winds for 30 seconds longer than predicted before burning up. This was a calculated sacrifice to protect moons that might hold life from the $3 billion spacecraft.
